old_title: Man Utd latest: Interest in Carrick replacement cools ahead of crunch Villa game
new_title: Man United latest: Carrick responds to uncertain future after unbelievable comeback

Manchester United host Aston Villa in the Premier League as under-fire manager Michael Carrick looks to build on their incredible comeback victory against Roma in midweek and stay in his job beyond the international break.
Carrick's side ended a nine-match winless run as they came from behind to beat Roma on Tuesday and they now face an Aston Villa team guided by a head coach in Unai Emery who looks set to reject the chance to move to Old Trafford in order to keep developing his new-look squad.
The subject of Carrick's future continues to dominate United's last match for two weeks, but The Independent reported that interest in Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, previously the two frontrunners for the job if Carrick is sacked, has cooled significantly.
It means United remain in limbo as they bid to respond to back-to-back Premier League defeats against Emery's side, who are unbeaten in five games in the division with in-form striker Nicolas Jackson scoring five goals in his last five.
Follow updates from Manchester United v Aston Villa in the Premier League, below
Man United dealt midfield set-back as Carlos Baleba potentially out until Christmas
Manchester United will be without Carlos Baleba for several weeks due to the hamstring injury he suffered against Roma.
United are waiting to discover if the £70m signing will play again this year as they are still to learn the full extent of his problem.
"We don't know, but it will be a number of weeks," said manager Michael Carrick, "It won't be after the international break [that Baleba returns]. It'll be a little bit longer than that."
The 22-year-old went off in tears after pulling up in the first minute of the second half on Tuesday and was not expected to be fit for Sunday's match against Aston Villa.
But now he is set to miss the trip to Anfield on 22 November and the Champions League game against Sporting CP three days later.
United face seven games in December, including a visit to Arsenal on December 20 and it is uncertain if Baleba will be fit in time to return then.
Baleba, who missed the start of the season with an ankle injury, has only started five games since his £70m move from Brighton.
Man Utd interest in Julian Nagelsmann cools 'significantly'
Julian Nagelsmann's stock has significantly dropped, meanwhile. While Manchester United's Christoph Vivell is said to be a fan, others in the hierarchy will be aware that Bayern Munich would not speak highly about his time there. The players didn't respond well to his approach or personality, and the image persists of Nagelsmann arriving to training on a skateboard. It is hard not to think of a line from The Sopranos. In the same way "a don doesn't wear shorts", a Manchester United manager doesn't have a skateboard.
Why Man United 'racked by indecision' over Michael Carrick future
Manchester United have been racked by indecision over the future of Michael Carrick. Numerous sources say there is a sense that no one was actually willing to make a call on the manager, a problem compounded by the fact they have "little idea" over a replacement.
In fairness, there are questions and debates over all of the main alternatives. United are understood to be much less sold on Eddie Howe than perception would have it. Sebastian Hoeness is highly rated, but his appointment would still involve a huge Ruben Amorim-like leap from Stuttgart. Fabian Hurzeler might struggle without Brighton's structure amid higher stakes, and there are doubts over whether United can even afford the compensation. Cesc Fabregas is impressing at Como but isn't going anywhere for now, and is viewed as Mikel Arteta's eventual successor at Arsenal.
Good afternoon and welcome
Manchester United remain in a 'will they, won't they' situation as they prepare to host Aston Villa in the Premier League and their last match before the international break.
Michael Carrick has so far survived the thrashing at Como, the humiliation at Bournemouth and the unravelling at Chelsea, while finally ending United's nine-match winless run by beating Roma in the Champions League in midweek.
But will that be enough? Or can Unai Emery's Aston Villa give United another day to forget and leave the Old Trafford hierarchy with a decision to make over the upcoming fortnight.

Michael Carrick said he still expects to be working with Manchester United over the international break and insisted he will not walk away after his players scored two stoppage-time goals to rescue an extraordinary 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in the Premier League.
The visitors appeared on course for a comfortable win after restoring their two-goal advantage in a crazy game Old Trafford, but late goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu saw United pull off their second great escape of the week after Tuesday's incredible comeback victory against Roma.
The result still leaves United in the Premier League's bottom three, however, and they will spend the international break 18th in the table before visiting rivals Liverpool. United have won just once in their first 10 in the Premier League, but Carrick was still applauded off the pitch by the United fans.
"We haven't won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on things that we've been working on and showing a lot of the good in the game today," Carrick said. "We need to tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches."
Villa boss Unai Emery was hugely frustrated to see his side twice throw away a two-goal lead, and stormed down the tunnel before full-time after Dorgu's equaliser. Villa were unhappy that United goalkeeper Senne Lammens appeared to prevent Zion Suzuki from catching the ball before Dorgu headed in.
Follow reaction from Manchester United v Aston Villa in the Premier League, below
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery storms down the tunnel after last-gasp Man United equaliser
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery appeared to storm off down the tunnel after Manchester United grabbed a last-gasp equaliser against his side to seal a remarkable 4-4 draw in one of the most chaotic Premier League games of the season.
In his post-match interview with Sky Sports, Emery suggested he simply left because United scored so late that he thought the match was essentially over.
Emery had already watched his side squander a 2-0 lead after the perfect start for the visiting Villans, with Alysson and Nicolas Jackson both finding the net inside the first five minutes.
'That's not going to happen': Michael Carrick will not walk away from Man Utd job
Michael Carrick said he still expects to be working with Manchester United over the international break and insisted he will not walk away after his players scored two stoppage-time goals to rescue an extraordinary 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in the Premier League.
The point means United sit 18th in the table, doing little to ease the intense scrutiny on Carrick given they are now eight league games without a win - a club record in the Premier League era - with their only victory of the season back in August against newly-promoted Ipswich.
Asked on Sky Sports if he would quit if he felt it was the right thing to do for the club, Carrick said: "That's not going to happen."
Then, speaking in his post-match press conference, Carrick expressed confidence his side could still turn things around this season.
"One hundred per cent," he said. "I think there's more than enough. Goals change games and we've got to deal with it and it's something we have to improve on drastically. But there's more than enough, we're just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times...
"I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in. We've just got to win games."
Man United's unique comeback leaves no one knowing how to feel
As the Manchester United players who had been told they were not fit to wear the shirt, in perhaps the earliest ever airing of that chant in footballing history, celebrated a second ridiculous comeback in five days, the Stretford End launched into a different chorus.
They had told the team they were unworthy of representing them after a mere five minutes, had jeered in damning fashion when the dreadful Diogo Dalot was substituted, had been vitriolic about the Glazer family, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox. But United left the pitch in the relegation zone while their supporters serenaded Michael Carrick.
"It's hard to believe it's not Scholes," they sang. In one respect, it was hard to believe it was not Sir Alex Ferguson, plucking results from nowhere. In another, it was hard to believe this was not the prelude to a sacking. It may still be.
Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa: Late goals complete another comeback
A huge cheer greeted Diogo Dalot's substitution and Old Trafford would empty as the clock wound down, only for those that stayed to be rewarded with a dramatic conclusion.
Mason Mount hit the crossbar and fellow sub Joshua Zirkzee pulled one back in stoppage time when turning home a Dorgu cross.Those remaining roared on the team and the sixth minute of stoppage time brought bedlam.
Dorgu rose to head home a Fernandes corner, with Suzuki's appeals he was upended trying to meet the cross ignored.
Under-fire Carrick left applauding fans chanting his name at the end of a crazy game, while Villa boss Emery was not there for the conclusion having stormed down the touchline after the leveller.
Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa: Another sloppy start from the hosts
Belief there could be a comeback like against Roma did not last long. Diogo Dalot's sloppy challenge on Alysson gave Villa a penalty that John McGinn coolly slotted home three minutes into the second half.
Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa: Youri Tielemans equalises against former club
Zion Suzuki brilliantly stopped a curling Cunha effort shortly after a mooted walkout failed to materialise, with Fernandes twice trying his luck as Kobbie Mainoo and Amad Diallo threatened.
Amad continued to prove a nuisance and United's hard work was rewarded just before half-time.
Tielemans' low strike from just inside the box beat Suzuki, whose appeals that his view was impeded by Bryan Mbeumo were immaterial as the forward was onside.
Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa: Bruno Fernandes sparks response
But then Tuesday's matchwinner Matheus Cunha to draw a foul from Boubacar Kamara in the box. Bruno Fernandes scored after the VAR ratified the on-field call, with the 16th-minute penalty sparking the best Premier League display from United since their solitary domestic win back in August.
Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa: Nicolas Jackson makes it two inside five
The mood darkened further in the fourth minute. Manchester United failed to deal with a free-kick and Alysson's strike was spilled by Senne Lammens, with Nicolas Jackson sweeping the ball into an empty net. "You're not fit to wear the shirt" bellowed home fans as Villa teased Carrick about his job prospects.
Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa: Alysson's opener inside 60 seconds
The change Manchester United fans really want goes far beyond the man in the dugout, as highlighted by the green and gold balloons that filled the air around a banner that read 'we don't want a new stadium, we want new owners'.
The furious chants against the Glazers, Ratcliffe and director of football Jason Wilcox went up a notch after Unai Emery's men capitalised on hodgepodge defending in the first minute.
The ball was played wide for Alysson and Dalot allowed him space to hit a first-time strike through Senne Lammens' legs.
Manchester United's run of slow starts
Manchester United have now gone five consecutive games where they have gone 2-0 down. This was the second time, after Roma in midweek, where they avoided defeat.
D: 4-4 v Aston Villa
W: 3-2 v Roma
L: 0-2 v Chelsea
L: 0-3 v Bournemouth
L: 1-4 v Como
